answer: Resist sybils with latency geolocation: each epoch a Yarrow-seeded beacon fires unpredictable pings from twelve known anchors, and every identity must answer inside its light-speed window. The round-trip vector triangulates a physical position, checked against the public anchor atlas; any two identities that resolve to the same coordinate collapse into one. A farm's clones share one haven, so they share one position, and to show 80 distinct locations it must rent 80 physically separated hosts, a cost that cannot be parallelized or bulk-bought from a single datacenter.
